semantic_correction.stem: The nurse receives report on four clients. Which client should the nurse assess first?

options.A: A client 2 hours after thyroidectomy who has new inspiratory stridor and increasing neck tightness.
options.B: A client with pneumonia who reports fatigue after walking to the bathroom and is now resting in bed.
options.C: A client with heart failure who has mild bilateral ankle edema unchanged from the prior assessment.
options.D: A client with diabetes who is waiting for discharge teaching about home glucose monitoring and diet.

semantic_correction.rationale: The 2026 NCSBN NCLEX-RN Test Plan directs the RN to establish priorities using pathophysiology and client acuity. NCBI/StatPearls identifies postoperative hemorrhage after thyroidectomy as a potentially life-threatening complication that can rapidly cause hematoma and airway compromise, and NCBI WebM&M describes neck tightness and stridor after thyroid surgery as warning findings of cervical hematoma and airway compromise that require prompt evaluation. Client A therefore has the highest-acuity airway threat and must be assessed first. The other clients have needs that require care, but the stem describes them as resting after exertion, unchanged from a prior assessment, or awaiting discharge teaching rather than having a new threat to airway or breathing. Therefore A is the uniquely best answer.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: When prioritizing multiple clients, assess a client with new postoperative stridor and neck tightness first because these findings can indicate rapidly progressive airway compromise after thyroid surgery.
semantic_correction.source_organization: NCBI Bookshelf / StatPearls; NCBI Bookshelf WebM&M; National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)

semantic_correction.source_locator: StatPearls Thyroidectomy > Complications — postoperative hemorrhage may rapidly produce hematoma and airway compromise. WebM&M Respiratory Distress after Neck Surgery > Commentary — cervical hematoma can cause rapid stridor and airway collapse; neck tightness/swelling and stridor are warning manifestations and prompt evaluation is necessary. NCSBN 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan > Management of Care > Establishing Priorities, printed p. 21 / PDF p. 25 — apply pathophysiology when establishing priorities for multiple clients and prioritize care based on acuity.

semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup: retired a managerial charge-nurse assignment item with weak distractors and a uniquely longest correct answer. Rebuilt the UID into a direct bedside multiple-client prioritization item centered on recognition of an acute postoperative airway threat.

audit_findings_append.finding: The replacement tests entry-level bedside prioritization rather than staffing management. New post-thyroidectomy stridor and neck tightness create a source-supported acute airway threat that clearly outranks the other explicitly stable/non-urgent client needs.
audit_findings_append.source_authority: NCBI Bookshelf / StatPearls; NCBI WebM&M; NCSBN 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan
audit_findings_append.source_locator: Thyroidectomy > Complications; Respiratory Distress after Neck Surgery > Commentary; NCSBN Establishing Priorities printed p. 21 / PDF p. 25

scope_exclusions.hematoma_diagnosis: The item does not require the nurse to establish a definitive hematoma diagnosis. The tested decision is priority assessment of a client with source-supported postoperative airway-warning findings.
scope_exclusions.emergency_procedure_sequence: The item asks which client to assess first and does not prescribe wound opening, intubation, oxygen flow rate, or another emergency procedure sequence.
scope_exclusions.other_client_diagnoses: The distractor clients are described only to establish current acuity. No universal claim is made that pneumonia, heart failure, or diabetes are inherently low priority.
scope_exclusions.timing_precision: The two-hour postoperative timing is scenario context and is not used as a universal threshold for hematoma occurrence or mandatory monitoring.

near_duplicate_check.note: Targeted GitHub searches for 'thyroidectomy stridor' and 'stridor postoperative assess first' returned no indexed repository match. No broad bank rescan was performed.

option_audit.A: Correct. New post-thyroidectomy stridor and increasing neck tightness indicate an acute airway-warning pattern requiring prompt evaluation.
option_audit.B: Plausible because pneumonia can deteriorate, but this client is described as fatigued after activity and now resting, without a new airway or breathing emergency in the stem.
option_audit.C: Plausible because heart failure can worsen, but the edema is explicitly mild and unchanged from the prior assessment, making it lower acuity than a new airway threat.
option_audit.D: Plausible because discharge teaching is necessary, but it is not more urgent than assessment of a new postoperative airway-warning sign.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible best answer. A has a new postoperative airway-warning pattern. B is resting after exertion, C is unchanged from baseline, and D is awaiting teaching. The stem therefore supplies a clear acuity hierarchy without requiring hidden assumptions.

cueing_check.note: Exact character counts were calculated from the stored strings. All four choices are within one character and use parallel client-description phrasing.

blueprint_audit.entry_level_relevance: NCSBN explicitly requires the RN to apply pathophysiology and acuity when establishing priorities among multiple clients. The rebuilt item tests a direct bedside prioritization decision.
